Question: Do agents understand and optimise their own cost: model selection, token budgets, tool call costs, compute time? Do they make explicit cost-quality tradeoffs?
Response: Yes. Cost optimisation is architectural. Skills specify the appropriate model tier for each task: cheap fast models for keyword filtering and triage, mid-tier models for routine reasoning, frontier models only for high-value decisions (top-30 candidate evaluation, complex compliance analysis). APIM AI Gateway enforces token budgets per agent per model. OTEL telemetry captures cost-per-phase with full attribution. The agentic loop itself can reason about cost-quality tradeoffs when the skill instructs it to — e.g. 'use the fast model for initial screening, escalate to frontier model only for borderline candidates.' Crystallised skills bypass the LLM entirely, executing at near-zero inference cost. The Fleet Manager tracks cost trends and flags anomalies — unexpected cost spikes trigger alerts on the Control Plane.
Key Technologies: Tiered Foundry models, APIM token budgets, OTEL cost attribution, skill-level model selection, crystallisation
POC Demo: POC1: Show cost dashboard — per-invoice cost breakdown with model tier attribution. Show cost reduction from crystallised vs generative skill execution.

Question: Can agents prioritise by value, not just urgency? Can they reason about downstream economic impact of delay?
Response: The Fleet Manager agent reasons about prioritisation across the fleet. Priority signals include: (1) Business value — invoice amount, candidate seniority, client tier. (2) SLA urgency — deadline proximity. (3) Downstream impact — the Fleet Manager can reason about dependencies (delaying budget approval blocks 3 downstream phases). (4) Cost of delay — configurable per workflow type (client-facing work has higher delay cost than internal admin). The Fleet Manager composes the prioritised exception queue using these signals, surfacing highest-value items first. This is not a pre-built opportunity cost calculator — it is the Fleet Manager agent's reasoning over workflow metadata and business rules encoded in its skills. The sophistication of economic reasoning depends on the business rules configured in the Fleet Manager's skills.
Key Technologies: Fleet Manager agent (value-based prioritisation), workflow metadata, configurable business rules

Question: Do agents respect SLA hierarchies; allocating premium compute to client-facing work and economy resources to internal admin?
Response: Yes. APIM AI Gateway supports priority-based model routing. Client-facing workflows can be tagged with a priority level in their workflow metadata. APIM policies route high-priority workflows to dedicated model deployments with guaranteed capacity, while internal admin workflows use shared capacity with lower priority. The Durable Functions orchestration respects priority in scheduling: high-priority phases are triggered immediately, while low-priority phases can be batched or deferred during peak load. Skills can specify compute requirements: 'this screening task is client-facing, use frontier model with dedicated capacity' vs 'this internal reconciliation can use shared economy compute.' The Fleet Manager monitors SLA compliance across the fleet and alerts operators when high-priority workflows risk SLA breach.
Key Technologies: APIM priority-based routing, Durable Functions scheduling, workflow priority metadata, Fleet Manager SLA monitoring
POC Demo: POC1: Show differentiated compute allocation — high-value client invoice processed with frontier model, routine internal reconciliation with economy model.

Question: Can each agent type produce periodic cost/value reports: cost, tasks handled, human-hours saved, quality score; aggregable for executive reporting?
Response: Yes. ROI reporting is built from OTEL telemetry and APIM metrics. Per-skill metrics: (1) Cost — total inference cost, tool call cost, compute cost per task, aggregated by skill, workflow type, market, and time period. Sourced from APIM token metrics and OTEL cost attribution. (2) Tasks handled — workflow completion counts and throughput metrics from Durable Functions telemetry. (3) Human-hours saved — calculated from workflow completion time vs baseline manual process time (configured per workflow type). (4) Quality score — Foundry Evaluator scores per skill, human override rates from the action ledger. The Control Plane provides a cost dashboard with per-workflow cost attribution. End-of-workflow ROI reports are generated by an agentic loop that queries telemetry data and produces structured analysis. Reports are aggregable for executive reporting via Application Insights workbooks or Power BI dashboards consuming the same data.
Key Technologies: OTEL cost attribution, APIM metrics, Foundry Evaluators, Application Insights workbooks, Power BI
POC Demo: POC1: Show end-of-workflow ROI report — cost per invoice, time saved vs manual process, quality score. Aggregated view across 30-50 workflows.
